claims.claim: Avoid long read-aloud passages in which NPCs carry on while the players sit idle; insert breaks for reactions.
claims.source: Living Greyhawk, Intro to Writing: Dire Boxed Text (Craig Heir, RPGA/WotC, 2004-04-13)
claims.quote: this is roleplaying not story time
claims.page: RPGA editor column on WotC site (read via Wayback)

claims.claim: Balance the amount of boxed text by running adventures to learn what is essential and cutting the rest; too much constrains the GM, too little strands them.
claims.source: Living Greyhawk, Intro to Writing: Dire Boxed Text (Craig Heir, RPGA/WotC, 2004-04-13)
claims.quote: Get a feel for what is bare-bones essential
claims.page: RPGA editor column on WotC site (read via Wayback)

claims.claim: A consistent style across RPGA adventures lets judges find information quickly; content and style rules live in the Living Greyhawk Writer's Guidelines.
claims.source: Living Greyhawk, Intro to Writing: Editor's Pen (Craig Heir, 2004-10-06)
claims.quote: allows judges to quickly find information they need
claims.page: RPGA editor column on WotC site (read via Wayback)

claims.claim: RPGA adventure content must stay PG-13 because children play the game.
claims.source: Living Greyhawk, Intro to Writing: Editor's Pen (Craig Heir, 2004-10-06)
claims.page: RPGA editor column on WotC site (read via Wayback)

claims.claim: Dungeon's read-aloud text gives a bare-bones description of the area and makes no reference to the viewer; 'you see' and 'as you enter the room' are banned.
claims.source: Dungeon Submission Guidelines (Dungeon staff, Paizo, 3.5 era)
claims.quote: it does not make any reference to the viewer

claims.claim: Creatures are excluded from read-aloud text because their positions and activities depend on circumstances such as whether they heard the PCs.
claims.source: Dungeon Submission Guidelines (Dungeon staff, Paizo, 3.5 era)
claims.quote: avoid including descriptions of any creatures in the room

claims.feature: few-sentence cap, handouts for the rest
claims.claim: Read-aloud text should only rarely exceed a few sentences; anything longer belongs in a player handout.
claims.source: Dungeon Submission Guidelines (Dungeon staff, Paizo, 3.5 era)
claims.quote: should only rarely run more than a few sentences

claims.claim: Encounters are keyed with labeled sections in a fixed order (Read-aloud Text, General Description, Creature(s), Tactics, Trap(s), Treasure, Development) and unneeded sections are omitted rather than filled.
claims.source: Dungeon Submission Guidelines (Dungeon staff, Paizo, 3.5 era)
claims.quote: The editors greatly dislike printing the words "This room is empty"

claims.claim: The Adventure Background is capped at 5% of total length, with adventures running 5,000-15,000 words and about 10,000 preferred.
claims.source: Dungeon Submission Guidelines (Dungeon staff, Paizo, 3.5 era)
claims.quote: no more than 5% of the total length

claims.claim: The mandatory synopsis must outline surprises and plot twists for the DM at the start rather than springing them during the adventure.
claims.source: Dungeon Submission Guidelines (Dungeon staff, Paizo, 3.5 era)
claims.quote: Outline surprises and plot twists here

claims.claim: Sidebars are kept to a minimum and capped at 300 words because they take more page space than their word count suggests.
claims.source: Dungeon Submission Guidelines (Dungeon staff, Paizo, 3.5 era)
claims.quote: no more than 300 words in length

claims.claim: Queries and adventures must condense backstory in favour of PC involvement; how the adventure plays decides acceptance.
claims.source: Dungeon Submission Guidelines (Dungeon staff, Paizo, 3.5 era)
claims.quote: an adventure is not a short story

claims.claim: Dragon refused articles written in the first person; 'I' and 'my' may appear only in a character's speech.
claims.source: Dragon Writers' Guidelines (Dragon staff, Paizo, 3.5 era)
claims.quote: we will not publish an article written in the first person

claims.claim: An opening narrative vignette or example dialogue may run no more than 200 words.
claims.source: Dragon Writers' Guidelines (Dragon staff, Paizo, 3.5 era)

claims.claim: Writers are told to avoid passive writing and 'to be' verbs in particular.
claims.source: Dragon Writers' Guidelines (Dragon staff, Paizo, 3.5 era)
claims.quote: Especially avoid passive writing, particularly "to be" verbs
